results.label: this tree ships the M110 news-window module (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
a release 20 minutes ahead is not reached by the 15-minute block when the feed is fetched
ten minutes later the SAME cached feed blocks that same release on the before side, with the offset re-measured to 10
so the window is applied at the check, not frozen at fetch time: the release crossed the 15-minute boundary while nothing about the feed changed
twenty minutes after that same release printed, and after the app re-read the feed, it is STILL a blackout — now on the after side and judged by the 45-minute settle
the blackout text says which side carried it and how long ago it printed
a blackout is not “sticky”: the sentence is rebuilt from this check’s offsets rather than remembered
fifty minutes after it printed the same release is clear at last, so the settle ends rather than accumulating
under 15/45 a release that printed 100 minutes ago is clear
the very next check uses the new pair, with no cache bust and no “applies tomorrow” freeze: 60/240 catches the 100-minute-old release
and the answer says where the numbers came from — `current` (the pair in force, read from the account) when the request overrides nothing, `request` when it does
nothing in the rule or its note claims a freeze, a next-day application or a per-day snapshot, because there is none
the guardrail day snapshot has no news column and its module never mentions the pair, so a news pair can never be frozen by the mechanism that freezes the caps
changing the trader’s display timezone changes nothing about the news verdict: same events, same offsets, same two numbers
a UTC day boundary cannot move the window either: the rule takes a single instant plus an event instant and never a date
planning and testing leave the account row exactly as it was: the read path cannot write back a “resolved” pair
and every read of the same row yields the same pair twice in a row, with nothing cached inside the module

scope: M110 freshness: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock and a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser; two asymmetric news clocks, no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
